newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian opposition worries violence may escalate.
newsitem.headline: Serbian opposition worries violence may escalate.

text.p: A Serbian opposition leader said on Tuesday he is worried that a hardline socialist party wants to escalate violence and impose a state of emergency in the country's 10-week political crisis.
"Until now, fortunately, (violence) has been isolated," Vuk Draskovic, a co-leader of the Zajedno (Together) coalition, told a news conference.

"But I am very afraid of the existence of a strategy of JUL, not of the Socialist Party, to provoke bloodshed in Serbia as a base for a state of emergency, as a base for some kind of military or police coup d'etat," Draskovic said.
He was referring to the Yugoslav United Left (JUL), headed by President Slobodan Milosevic's wife, Mirjana Markovic, which is joined in coalition with the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS).

"JUL is a real terrorist organisation and JUL is using this political crisis to achieve two goals at the same time -- eliminate the democratic, pro-European coalition Zajedno and at the same time the Socialist Party of Serbia and to take power, a real communist power," Draskovic said.

Draskovic said there were still "reasonable people" in the governing SPS but they were afraid to speak out against the government's decision annulling Zajedno victories in 14 cities, including Belgrade, in November municipal elections.

The Zajedno victories have been confirmed by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, and Western countries led by the United States have urged Milosevic to reinstate the results, but so far the government has refused to budge.

The opposition has held daily demonstrations for 10 weeks to force the government's hand and has now resorted to a new tactic, initiated in the town of Smederevska Palanka 80 km (50 miles) south of Belgrade, of installing parallel governments.
Draskovic said that if setting up a parallel council worked there, Zajedno could consider doing the same in Belgrade.
"Maybe we've got today an example of what can we do, just to constitute on the streets," he said.
"They did it in Smederevska Palanka (after all). They respected the law, the election results from November 17," he said.

Draskovic said Zajedno planned to pursue all legal channels to force the government to recognise its victories across the country and in Belgrade, where a district court on Monday dismissed appeals of an electoral commission and upheld earlier rulings that Socialist had won.
"There are still a few legal possibilities to implement the recommendation of the electoral commission to reinstate the election results from November 17," Draskovic said.

"I...hope that within the next few days the regime will realise the necessity of full implementation of election results from November 17. And our protest demonstrations will increase every day...to protect our election results."
